_anchors.canvas.w: 32 = the Stardew cell. This sample is the control: if the control does not clear, the round already answered everything.
_anchors.canvas.originY: canvas.h * 0.56, so the arthropod's legs land inside the frame at body.scale 0.7
_anchors.tones.perMaterial: 3, the low end of the knob's 3-6 range (BACKLOG). Cohesion over virtuosity is the idiom's whole claim.
_anchors.frames.walk: 4, the Stardew walk cycle. Also the floor set by the gait: the four named phases sit at 0, 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4, so a cycle must carry a multiple of 4 frames or a key pose lands between frames and is never seen.
_anchors.light.x: unit vector from the upper left, held identical across all four probe samples so lighting is never the variable
_anchors.light.curve: 1.9. At 3 tones a linear ramp gives the shadow a third of the sprite and the silhouette dies in it; 1.9 pushes the dark tone down to a rim and leaves the two light tones to carry the form.
_anchors.light.y: the y half of light.x's unit vector
_anchors.outline.enabled: on: at 32 px an outline is what keeps the silhouette from dissolving into the background
_anchors.outline.inner: on: at 32 px, two parts of one material that touch read as one mass, and shading cannot separate them because shading is continuous across the seam
_anchors.outline.rim: off. The silhouette edge by value instead of line - a rim on the lit side, an occlusion edge on the shadow side. This is the knob the silhouette round is comparing against outline.enabled, and it is off in every sample that predates the round.
_anchors.body.scale: 0.7 = 32/48, the canvas ratio against the grammar's authored size. Shapes are analytic, so this re-rasterises rather than resamples.
_anchors.gait.swing: 0.07 turn, derived from the 7 px femur: a foot travel of about 3 px, which is the largest step 32 px can show without the legs leaving the body
_anchors.gait.lift: 1.2 px = thorax height (2 * ry = 10) / 8, the same eighth-of-the-body rule used in every sample
_anchors.texture.speckle: 0: the control idiom spends nothing on texture
_anchors.playback.msPerFrame: 150 ms. 4 frames x 150 = a 600 ms cycle, and all four probe samples complete a cycle in 600 ms so the sheet never compares walking speed. 600 was chosen over 500 because it divides into whole milliseconds for 4, 8 and 12 frames, and the export contract has no room for a fractional frame duration.
_anchors.playback.scale: 6, because 32 x 6 = 192 px on screen - the same cell size as every other sample, which is the only way two resolutions compare as idioms
